name: CELL
description: CELL returns information about the formatting, location, or contents of a cell, selected by the info_type argument (e.g. "address", "contents", "row", "col", "format", "type", "filename").
tldr: Returns information about a cell (address, contents, format, etc.).

parameters.name: info_type
parameters.description: A quoted text string naming the info to return, such as "address", "contents", "row", "col", "width", "format", "type", or "filename".

parameters.name: reference
parameters.description: The cell or range to inspect. If omitted, CELL uses the last cell that was changed.

basicExample.description: Get the absolute address of a cell
basicExample.explanation: The "address" info type returns the absolute reference of the cell.

advancedExamples.title: Read a cell's contents
advancedExamples.description: Return the value held in a cell
advancedExamples.explanation: The "contents" info type returns the value stored in the referenced cell.

advancedExamples.title: Get the row number
advancedExamples.scenario: Find which row a cell is on.
advancedExamples.explanation: The "row" info type returns the row number of the reference.

howItWorks: CELL returns a single piece of information about a cell chosen by info_type. Common types include "address" (absolute reference as text), "contents" (the cell's value), "row"/"col" (row/column numbers), "width" (column width), "format" (a code describing number format), "type" (b/l/v for blank/label/value), and "filename" (the full path and sheet). If reference is omitted, CELL refers to the last cell changed, which is unpredictable.

howToSteps.name: Choose info_type
howToSteps.text: Decide what you need, e.g. "address" or "row".

limitations: Volatile: CELL recalculates on every change, which can slow large workbooks.
If reference is omitted, it refers to the last changed cell, which is unpredictable.
'filename' returns an empty string if the workbook has not been saved.

commonErrors.cause: An invalid info_type string was supplied.
commonErrors.fix: Use a valid code such as "address", "row", or "format".

commonErrors.cause: CELL('filename') result is cached until recalculation.
commonErrors.fix: Press F9 to recalculate and refresh the value.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: CELL exists in Google Sheets but supports only a subset of info_type values (e.g. "address", "row", "col", "content", "width", "height", "format", "bgcolor", "fontcolor"); "filename" and "type" behave differently or are unsupported.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Not all Excel info_type codes are available in Sheets; check support for the specific code.

faq.question: Is CELL volatile?
faq.answer: Yes, it recalculates on every change to the workbook.

faq.question: What does "type" return?
faq.answer: 'b' for blank, 'l' for label (text), or 'v' for value (number/date).

faq.question: How do I get the file path?
faq.answer: Use =CELL("filename", A1), which returns something like C:[book.xlsx]Sheet1!A1.
